slokas.title: Karmanyevadhikaraste (Chapter 2, Verse 47)
slokas.sanskritText:
कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन।
मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि॥
slokas.transliteration:
karmaṇy-evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana |
mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo 'stvakarmaṇi ||
slokas.englishMeaning: You have a right to perform your prescribed duties, but you are not entitled to the fruits of your actions. Never consider yourself the cause of the results of your activities, nor be attached to inaction.

questions.questionText: According to Bhagavad Gita 2.47, what does one have the primary right to?
questions.explanation: Karmaṇy-evādhikāras te translates to "You have a right only to work/duty".

questions.questionText: What attitude towards inaction (akarmaṇi) is advised in this verse?
questions.explanation: The verse states "mā te saṅgo 'stvakarmaṇi" — do not be attached to inaction.

slokas.title: Yada Yada Hi Dharmasya (Chapter 4, Verse 7)
slokas.sanskritText:
यदा यदा हि धर्मस्य ग्लानिर्भवति भारत।
अभ्युत्थानमधर्मस्य तदात्मानं सृजाम्यहम्॥
slokas.transliteration:
yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati bhārata |
abhyutthānam adharmasya tadātmānaṁ sṛjāmy aham ||
slokas.englishMeaning: Whenever and wherever there is a decline in religious practice, O descendant of Bharata, and a predominant rise of irreligion—at that time I descend Myself.

questions.questionText: When does the Lord descend according to Chapter 4, Verse 7?
options: Whenever there is a decline in Dharma and rise in Adharma
At the beginning of every spring season
questions.explanation: Yadā yadā hi dharmasya glānir bhavati indicates whenever Dharma declines.

questions.questionText: What does the word "Glāniḥ" signify in this sloka?
questions.explanation: Glānir means decline or degeneration of Dharma.

slokas.title: Paritranaya Sadhunam (Chapter 4, Verse 8)
slokas.sanskritText:
परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्।
धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय सम्भवामि युगे युगे॥
slokas.transliteration:
paritrāṇāya sādhūnāṁ vināśāya ca duṣkṛtām |
dharma-saṁsthāpanārthāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge ||
slokas.englishMeaning: To deliver the pious and to annihilate the miscreants, as well as to reestablish the principles of religion, I appear millenium after millenium.

questions.questionText: What is the triple purpose of divine descent in this sloka?
options: Protect the virtuous, eliminate wrongdoers, re-establish righteousness
Accumulate power, rule kingdoms, punish citizens
Build temples, write scriptures, conduct debates
Travel the worlds, test devotion, grant wealth

slokas.title: Patram Pushpam Phalam Toyam (Chapter 9, Verse 26)
slokas.sanskritText:
पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति।
तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः॥
slokas.transliteration:
patraṁ puṣpaṁ phalaṁ toyaṁ yo me bhaktyā prayacchati |
tad ahaṁ bhakty-upahṛtam aśnāmi prayatātmanaḥ ||
slokas.englishMeaning: If one offers Me with love and devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, I will accept it.

questions.questionText: What key ingredient makes an offering acceptable according to Chapter 9 Verse 26?
questions.explanation: Yo me bhaktyā prayacchati — offered with sincere devotion.

slokas.title: Ananyas Chintayanto Mam (Chapter 9, Verse 22)
slokas.sanskritText:
अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते।
तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम्॥
slokas.transliteration:
ananyāś cintayanto māṁ ye janāḥ paryupāsate |
teṣāṁ nityābhiyuktānāṁ yoga-kṣemaṁ vahāmy aham ||
slokas.englishMeaning: To those who are constantly devoted and who meditate on My transcendental form, I supply what they lack and preserve what they have.

questions.questionText: What does "Yoga-Kṣemam" refer to in Chapter 9, Verse 22?
options: Providing what is needed and preserving what is acquired
questions.explanation: Yoga means acquiring necessary goods and Kshema means safeguarding what has been attained.

slokas.title: Manmana Bhava Madbhakto (Chapter 18, Verse 65)
slokas.sanskritText:
मन्मना भव मद्भक्तो मद्याजी मां नमस्कुरु।
मामेवैष्यसि सत्यं ते प्रतिजाने प्रियोऽसि मे॥
slokas.transliteration:
man-manā bhava mad-bhakto mad-yājī māṁ namaskuru |
mām evaiṣyasi satyaṁ te pratijāne priyo 'si me ||
slokas.englishMeaning: Always think of Me, become My devotee, worship Me and offer your homage unto Me. Thus you will come to Me without fail. I promise you this because you are My very dear friend.

questions.questionText: What four practices are outlined in Chapter 18, Verse 65?
options: Fix mind on the Divine, become devoted, worship, offer obeisance
Give charity, construct monuments, memorize words, isolate
questions.explanation: Man-manā (think of Me), mad-bhakto (be My devotee), mad-yājī (worship Me), māṁ namaskuru (bow to Me).
